text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Removing flood damage will require spending of at least four billion zlotys from the public budget, the opposition left-wing Union of Labour (UP) party said, while the centrist Union for Freedom (UW) has said businesses operating in flooded areas need to be supported.
- Wojciech Kornowski, the president of Korvita hospital in Poznan, Poland's biggest private hospital, will run for the senate in September's parliamentary elections, Kornowski said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Retail and wholesale commercial activity accounted for 82 percent of all the revenues of small and medium size businesses in 1996, a report by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
Service sales by industrial, construction and transport firms accounted for the rest.
- Britain's Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc. is planning to buy into the Heros SA insurance firm, a source who declined to be named said.
- The Stovit vegetable and fruit processing firm plans to construct a new plant in Bydgoszcz province, western Poland, worth $3 million, Stovit's president Antoni Kisielewski said.
- Widening the scope of obligatory insurance schemes will allow the repaying of flood related damage in southern Poland, the state-owned PZU insurer's president Jan Monkiewicz said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The listed Ampli, Energomontaz Poludnie, Polar and PLI firms will start their share issues on the primary market on Monday.
- The WKSM aggregate mine in Wroclaw, southwestern Poland, will start trade on the Warsaw bourse parallel market on Monday.
- Poland's 1997 grain harvest will yield up to 24.8 million tonnes, a decline by around 1.7 million tonnes, a preliminary forecast by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Pepsico Restaurants International have opened Pizza Hut's twenty-ninth outlet in Poland, Pepsico said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The number of retail outlets has declined by 20,000 in 1996 as a result of international supermarket chains' development in Poland, a report by GUS showed.
ZYCIE
- Poland's bicycle production has declined by between 30 percent and 50 percent as a result of cheap bicycle imports from China and Taiwan.
- The number of tractors used by Poland's farmers grew by 1.3 million in the period from 1987 to 1996, showing a 25 percent increase over the decade, a report by GUS said.
- The Lucent Technologies and Alcatel telecoms equipment makers each account for 40 percent of new equipment deliveries to telecoms monopolist Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA).
